newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to ask local funds to shore up exchange.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to ask local funds to shore up exchange.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda said on Tuesday that he would ask local mutual funds and market rescue funds operated by the government and private sector to shore up the battered local stock market.

"I will ask mutual funds to take care of the market. The market is likely to normalise after that. I believe foreign selling is only portfolio adjustment," he told reporters after a meeting of finance ministry, central bank and stock market officials.

He added that money from a 15.7 billion baht (US$628 million) fund, set up several months ago and operated by bankers and brokers, as well as a 10 billion baht finance ministry fund established in August would be used to revive the flagging market.

News that the funds would enter the market boosted sentiment on Tuesday, pushing the stock index into positive territory after it had languished in the negative zone earlier in the day. The SET index, which plummeted 6.0 percent on Monday to a more than three-year low was trading at 956.34 points at 0933 GMT, against the day's low of 919.52.
